84cc710542.q: What does Harvard research say about the connection between gratitude and happiness?
84cc710542.a: According to Harvard research cited in positive psychological studies, gratitude is strongly and consistently associated with greater happiness. Gratitude helps people feel more positive emotions, relish good experiences, improve their health, and deal with adversity while building strong relationships.

beb68a3373.q: What are practical daily exercises to practice gratitude mentioned in the Broker to Broker Real Estate Podcast?
beb68a3373.a: The episode recommends several daily gratitude exercises: maintaining a gratitude journal each morning or evening, creating gratitude videos for social media platforms like YouTube or TikTok, practicing morning meditation focused on reflection and calm, volunteering in your community, and implementing a gratitude box in your office where employees can anonymously express appreciation for colleagues.

cc4a49c1a4.q: How can gratitude impact mental and physical health according to real estate leadership research?
cc4a49c1a4.a: Gratitude can be beneficial not only to physical health but also extremely helpful to mental health. It helps offset potential burnout leaders may experience, improves sleep quality, allows better planning and hopes for the future, and deepens relationships with those around you.

d48efd0474.q: How did Jackie Liberto grow her real estate brokerage to 119 agents in 19 months while retaining all but seven agents?
d48efd0474.a: Jackie Liberto retained 112 of 119 agents by focusing on authentic engagement and holistic care—supporting agents' personal health, family health, and business health. Of the seven who left, two exited real estate entirely and two left for personal reasons unrelated to the brokerage. She emphasizes caring about individuals as people first rather than prioritizing production numbers, using a mentoring program that compresses the first six months into 60 days and implementing systematic onboarding via Asana with regular four-to-six-week new agent orientations.
d48efd0474.e: B2B 37: How to Retain Agents in Your Organization

0778356f51.q: What is the Emerald Coast Agent Panel and how has it impacted agent recruitment and community engagement?
0778356f51.a: The Emerald Coast Agent Panel is a quarterly open-forum event that began in December 2020 after Jackie Liberto's top producers reported increased networking interest. Held at a local church venue with capacity for over 100 people, it features panels of top producers, lenders, and title company professionals—including external speakers like Brent Scott—and is open to all industry professionals, buyers, and sellers. Starting in 2022, it expanded to include breakout panels and half-day training sessions every other month, with no company recruitment messaging, focusing purely on community value and industry collaboration.
0778356f51.e: B2B 37: How to Retain Agents in Your Organization

b5d243302c.q: What onboarding and mentoring system does Jackie Liberto use to prevent new agents from falling through the cracks?
b5d243302c.a: Jackie Liberto uses Asana for systematic onboarding with every staff member assigned a role in the process. New agents undergo a four-to-six-week orientation returning to day-one checklist items to ensure no steps are missed. Mentorship is handled by two people—Jackie herself and an agent named Tanya—who conduct weekly two-hour Monday meetings, provide phone and FaceTime support, record all sessions for those unable to attend, and cycle through four training platforms on repeat with continuous feedback refinement.
b5d243302c.e: B2B 37: How to Retain Agents in Your Organization

2a35289635.q: How does Jackie Liberto's interview process for recruiting agents differ from traditional brokerage recruiting?
2a35289635.a: Rather than providing answers or directing conversation, Jackie begins interviews by asking 'Why are you here?' or 'Why now?'—seeking to understand each agent's specific pain points and motivations before tailoring her pitch. This approach reveals whether an agent is frustrated with other brokerages, seeking creative freedom, or responding to other drivers, allowing Jackie to address actual needs instead of assumptions. She emphasizes that agents want to be heard, and this initial listening sets the tone for a person-focused rather than production-focused relationship.
2a35289635.e: B2B 37: How to Retain Agents in Your Organization

55981304f4.q: What personal follow-up system does Jackie Liberto implement to support agents after they join her brokerage?
55981304f4.a: Jackie sets calendar reminders and recurring events for each new agent to ensure she follows up every three days, monitoring their wellbeing and life circumstances. She connects with agents on Facebook to stay aware of challenges they share publicly, then reaches out proactively—for example, texting 'I know you had a tough week last week, are you feeling better?'—demonstrating authentic care that cannot be faked and that agents recognize immediately.
55981304f4.e: B2B 37: How to Retain Agents in Your Organization

0443b63056.q: What is Jackie Liberto's core philosophy on agent production versus agent wellbeing?
0443b63056.a: Jackie prioritizes agent wellness and personal happiness over production targets. She tells agents 'run your own race'—whether they want to close one transaction per month or ten—and commits to supporting any production level as long as agents are 'whole and happy and healthy.' She explicitly states in initial conversations that she cares more about them as individuals than their production numbers, a principle she calls 'retraining brains' to reset expectations from competitive brokerage cultures.
0443b63056.e: B2B 37: How to Retain Agents in Your Organization

2e9cbd54f4.q: What is the minimum investment amount to start with Secured Investment Corp's Regulation A-plus non-accredited investor fund?
2e9cbd54f4.a: The Regulation A-plus fund, which opened three years ago, is open to anybody with a $1,000 minimum investment. After the initial $1,000, investors can make additional investments in $1,000 increments, up to a maximum of 10% of their annual estimated income or 10% of their estimated assets, as regulated by the SEC.

4c299f3c9c.q: What historical returns can investors expect from Secured Investment Corp's residential real estate investment funds?
4c299f3c9c.a: The non-accredited investor fund has historically been paying out 8 to 10% annually. The funds have yielded 8 to 11% for the last eight years. Past performance is not a guarantee of future performance, but the organization maintained 10% to 11% payouts through the first year of COVID, which was maintained consistently.
4c299f3c9c.e: B2B 38: How to Create Passive Income from Commissions

62a242c3d2.q: How long is the lockup period for investments in Secured Investment Corp's funds, and what is the exit timeline?
62a242c3d2.a: Investors must remain in the fund for a minimum of one year (12-month tie-up period). If divesting after that first year, the exit process takes another 12 months—investors receive 25% of their requested amount every quarter for four quarters. As stated by the fund manager: '12 months in, 12 months to get out.'
62a242c3d2.e: B2B 38: How to Create Passive Income from Commissions

0f0e3b2c9c.q: What are the SEC definitions of accredited versus non-accredited investors for purposes of investment fund participation?
0f0e3b2c9c.a: Accredited investors must meet one of two criteria: either have $1 million in assets (excluding primary residence equity) with net assets exceeding liabilities, or earn $200,000 annually as a single person or $300,000 as a married couple for the last two consecutive years. Non-accredited investors do not meet these thresholds but can access non-accredited funds with investment caps of 10% of annual income or assets.

d2586cc85c.q: How does Secured Investment Corp's business model differ from Wall Street-dependent private lenders, particularly regarding funding stability?
d2586cc85c.a: Secured Investment Corp does not leverage funds, rely on lines of credit, or depend on Wall Street money. Instead, it works with one-off lenders and investors who directly fund the operations. During COVID, many Wall Street-dependent lenders shut down overnight when funders demanded capital back, but Secured Investment Corp continued lending and paying 10% to 11% returns throughout the pandemic because it relied on individual investors rather than Wall Street capital.
d2586cc85c.e: B2B 38: How to Create Passive Income from Commissions

f90bc72dba.q: What is the focus market segment for Secured Investment Corp's lending and investment activities?
f90bc72dba.a: Secured Investment Corp focuses exclusively on the affordable housing market, specifically properties under the FHA cap (which varies by county). The company lends on and purchases single-family to four-unit properties that are non-owner occupied for investment purposes. They avoid high-end properties because they have limited buyer databases and poor returns on investment.
